aiOverview.content: Know a tornado is near by looking for a roaring sound (like a freight train), a visible rotating funnel cloud, or a low-hanging cloud of debris. Other warning signs include a dark green or black sky, large hail followed by calm, or intense, fast-moving clouds. Immediately take shelter if you hear sirens, receive a Wireless Emergency Alert (WEA) on your phone, or hear a tornado warning on a NOAA Weather Radio. Wireless Emergency Alert (WEA) tornado warning NOAA Weather Radio Key Warning Signs Sound: A loud, continuous roar or rumble that doesn't fade, similar to a freight train or jet engine. Visual Clues: A visible rotating funnel cloud, a wall cloud, or a cloud of debris moving along the ground. Sky Color: The sky may turn a dark, greenish, or black color. Atmosphere: Calmness followed by intense, rapid wind shifts, heavy rain, or large hail. Movement: If a tornado is spotted and appears not to be moving right or left, it may be moving directly toward you. How to Receive Alerts Phones: Ensure your mobile device is set to receive Wireless Emergency Alerts (WEA). Radio/TV: Local news and radio stations will break into programming. Weather Radio: A NOAA Weather Radio provides 24/7 alerts, even during power outages. NOAA Weather Radio Sirens: Outdoor sirens are designed to alert those outside, not inside homes. Apps: Use trusted weather apps for real-time tracking, such as Tornado HQ or TornadoPath. Tornado HQ TornadoPath If a warning is issued or danger is imminent, immediately get to a safe place—usually an interior room on the lowest floor of a sturdy building, such as a basement, bathroom, or closet.
